answer: Sybil resistance works when an identity cannot signal value without paying for it. The mechanism: each agent posts a slashable bond at registration, so a new identity costs real capital. Reputation accrues only via per-epoch attestations from established non-kin peers, so a clone's plume of self-declared credentials is worthless. Newcomers stay on a probation ledge, rate-limited and barred from high-value tasks until countersignatures accumulate. Double-signing or synchronized payloads trigger slashing, and the seized bond funds a bounty for the detecting watcher, making detection profitable.
